name: simplest-ai-sessions
description: The simplest AI session manager for VS Code — a local, passive monitor for Claude Code & Codex CLI sessions. No API keys, no LLM calls.

aiSessions.tmuxAutoAttach.description: Automatically open a terminal attached to any tmux session that hosts a Claude/Codex session and currently has no client attached. Closing that terminal only detaches; the tab is not re-opened for the same tmux session unless the session is re-created.

aiSessions.tmuxEnsure.markdownDescription: Keep these tmux sessions alive. When a listed `session` is missing, `command` runs in a new terminal named after the session (via `$SHELL -lc`). The command must be idempotent (e.g. `tmux new-session -A …`). Skipped while `offFile` exists. Put this in **workspace** settings so only that window does it.

command.description: Shell command that creates (or attaches to) the session

offFile.description: If this file exists, do nothing (pause switch)

aiSessions.startupLayout.enabled.markdownDescription: On every window start/reload, run `#aiSessions.startupLayout.commands#` in order, then focus the terminal named `#aiSessions.startupLayout.focusTerminal#`.

aiSessions.startupLayout.commands.description: VS Code command ids to run at startup, in order (e.g. workbench.action.closeAllEditors, aiSessions.sidebar.focus).

aiSessions.startupLayout.focusTerminal.description: Terminal name to show and focus after the startup commands (waits up to 30s for it to appear). Empty = none.

aiSessions.startupLayout.closeIdleTermin.description: After the startup commands, close terminals that were present at startup but hold only an idle shell (no child processes) and no AI session — e.g. empty shells restored after an app restart. Terminals created by this extension and any terminal running something are kept.
